tdb85ec26: Our school's computer lab is a core hub of educational activity, but it is also a major consumer of electrical energy. Every workstation consists of multiple components (the computer unit, the monitor, and peripheral accessories) that draw power constantly while in active use. More importantly, many IT devices continue to draw power even when they appear to be asleep or turned off—a phenomenon known as 'Vampire Power' or standby load.
t9f374d18: By conducting an energy audit of the school computer lab, we can quantify exactly how electricity is spent, calculate the financial costs incurred by the school, and identify targeted behavioral and technical strategies to dramatically decrease our environmental and budget footprint.
ta5da7bbf: **Power Rating (Wattage):** – The rate at which an electrical device consumes energy. It is measured in Watts (W). A higher wattage means a device requires more electricity per second to run.
t6623e478: **Energy Consumption:** – The total amount of electricity consumed over time. Electric utility companies measure and bill energy in Kilowatt-hours (kWh).
t535fac52: **Standby Load (Vampire Power):** – Power drawn by an electronic appliance while it is switched off or in a standby mode but remains plugged into a live socket.
tc302db8c: To perform energy audits, we use the following standard conversion equations:
t743ce811: Financial Cost (€) = Energy Consumption (kWh) × Electricity Tariff (€/kWh)
